title: Data Warehouse Testing/ETL Testing
description: Roles and Responsibilities * Lead end-to-end Data Warehouse Testing (DWT) initiatives across multiple projects, ensuring high data quality and integrity. * Design, plan, and execute test strategies and test plans for data warehouse and ETL components based on business and technical requirements. * Validate data mapping, data transformations, aggregations, and data movement from source to staging, DWH, and downstream systems. * Develop and maintain comprehensive test cases, test scenarios, and test data sets for DWT and ETL testing. * Perform functional, regression, system integration, and user acceptance support testing for data warehouse solutions. * Analyze complex SQL queries and datasets to identify data discrepancies, defects, and root causes. * Collaborate with ETL developers, data modelers, and business analysts to clarify requirements and resolve defects efficiently. * Establish and enforce quality standards, best practices, and processes for data testing within the team. * Provide technical leadership and mentoring to junior testers, guiding them on DWT and ETL testing techniques and tools. * Prepare clear test reports, defect metrics, and quality dashboards for stakeholders and project leadership. * Participate in design and code review discussions from a quality perspective, highlighting potential data quality risks. * Coordinate with cross-functional teams to ensure timely test execution and alignment with project timelines and release plans. * Position will be based on business requirements across locations. Job Description As a Quality Engineering Lead in Data Warehouse Testing, you will be at the heart of ensuring that business-critical data is accurate, reliable, and ready for insight-driven decisions. You will lead testing efforts across complex DWH and ETL ecosystems, collaborating closely with data engineers, BI developers, and business stakeholders to validate data flows end-to-end. This role offers the opportunity to shape test strategies, introduce best practices, and mentor a team of testers while working on large-scale, enterprise-grade data platforms.If you enjoy solving data quality challenges, designing robust test frameworks, and driving continuous improvement in a collaborative environment, this position will allow you to make a visible impact on how data powers the organization's success. Skills Technology->Data Integration and ETL->ETL - Foundation

description: Itron is innovating new ways for utilities and cities to manage energy and water. We create a more resourceful world to protect essential resources for today and tomorrow. Join us. These software and AI solutions solve end-to-end challenges for the utilities that power our society and are used by the largest and most complex organizations in the world such as National Grid, Southern Company, and Exelon. Itron Resiliency Solutions is a global, diverse team of builders and innovators who tackle previously impossible challenges for our customers. If you have a desire to challenge yourself, solve impactful problems, and work with a passionate and talented team, this is the place. About the role We're hiring an SDET-2 (Software Development Engineer in Test) in Bengaluru to own quality for the services our customers depend on. You'll decide what to test and how, build and maintain automation, test by hand where it finds problems fastest, and help the team ship often without breaking customers. Our India engineering team is taking full ownership of core products and growing quickly, including a ground-up rebuild of a customer-critical service. Quality is a first-class priority for us, not a phase at the end. You'll work closely with developers, Product, Customer Support and your Engineering Manager. What you'll own in your first year Own: Own quality for a service or product area end to end — test strategy, automation, release sign-off, and follow-up on escaped bugs. Test strategy. Decide what to automate, what to test by hand, and what risk is acceptable for each release. Automation that lasts. Build and extend API, UI and integration test suites that are fast, reliable and run in CI on every change. Shift left. Review designs and requirements early, and work with developers so testability is built in, not bolted on. Learn from escapes. When a bug reaches customers, find out why and close the gap so it doesn't happen again. Raise the bar. Review test code, mentor SDET-1s, and help interview candidates. What you must bring These are the bar. We can't teach them on the job. Experience: 2–5 years in software testing or development. We level on demonstrated scope, not years alone. You've built automation that runs in CI. Test suites you designed or substantially extended, that run on every change and that the team trusts. You own quality, not just test cases. You've decided what to test for a feature or release, and stood behind the call. You are comfortable testing by hand. You use manual and exploratory testing deliberately, where it finds problems faster than scripts. You work independently toward a clear goal. Given a feature or release, you plan the testing, unblock yourself, and raise risks early. Test plan Breakdown: You can take product requirements and create deep test plan including all corner cases to ensure Quality We care how you test more than which tool you did it in. Technical background You've tested production systems with a modern stack, such as: Languages: strong in at least one language such as Python, Java or JavaScript/TypeScript — you write test code with the same care as product code. Test automation: frameworks such as Pytest, JUnit/TestNG, Playwright, Cypress or Selenium, including structuring a suite so it stays maintainable. APIs and services: contract and integration testing of REST APIs, including error paths, auth and data validation. CI and cloud: running tests in CI pipelines, and testing services deployed on AWS — reading logs and metrics to diagnose failures. Databases: SQL to set up and verify data, and an understanding of how data issues show up as bugs. Non-functional testing: exposure to performance or load testing with tools such as JMeter, k6 or Locust. Exact tools matter less than depth. Strong experience on an equivalent stack is welcome. What sets great candidates apart Impact you can explain. Escaped bugs went down, release time went down, or flaky tests went away — and you can say what you did to get there. A suite you made better. You took slow or flaky automation and made it fast and trusted, not just bigger. Framework mindset: You spot repeated test code and turn it into reusable helpers, fixtures or tooling others build on. Root-cause thinking. You trace a failure to its cause in code, data or config, not just report the symptom. Product sense. You've pushed back on a release, or on a requirement that would confuse users, and been right. Lifting others. Test reviews, docs or mentoring that made developers and newer SDETs better at quality. What we look for in everyone we hire Whatever the role, we hire for six things. Customer obsession. You test the way customers actually work, and you treat every escaped bug and support ticket as a lesson. Impact over activity. You measure success by bugs that never reached customers and releases that went out smoothly, not test-case counts. Honesty. You report quality as it is, say clearly what wasn't tested, and raise release risks even when it's unwelcome. Independence. You don't wait to be told what to test. You find the risk worth covering and get it done with little hand-holding. You will work with leaders who will partner with you in the journey. Passion. Not the word on a resume — the evidence: a tool you built, a technique you went deep on, things you taught others. Depth. At least one system you've tested well enough to explain its internals, its failure modes and how you'd test them. Itron is committed to building an inclusive and diverse workforce and providing an authentic workplace experience for all employees. If you are excited about this role but your past experiences don't perfectly align with every requirement, we encourage you to apply anyway. In the end, you may be just who we are looking for! description: The Company PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy. We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers. We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade. Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities. Job Summary: Under summary section Zettle India, part of PayPal's Payment Services and Crypto organization, is hiring a Software Engineer in Test (SDET). Our POS platform moves real money for merchants every day across mobile apps, cloud services, and card readers. In this hands-on role, you'll turn designs into written risk models before code exists, build automated checks that gate real merges, and encode how the payments domain behaves so the knowledge outlives any one person. You'll help shape how test engineering works on a platform where quality is built in, not bolted on. If you'd rather build the thing than maintain it, read on — the best is yet to come! Job Description: Essential Responsibilities: Implements tasks within the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC), receiving structure and oversight from more experienced staff Follows well-established internal conventions and standard procedures Understands internal standards & processes an applies them to make technical decisions Collaborates with peers, manager, and project lead to gain understanding of tasks and review solutions May contribute to code & design reviews Minimum Qualifications: 1+ years relevant experience and a Bachelor’s degree OR Any equivalent combination of education and experience. Additional Responsibilities & Preferred Qualifications : What you need to know about the role: PayPal POS sits at the heart of how many SMBs run their businesses every day. Card payments, card readers and hardware variance, acquiring, payments SDKs, ledger and financial flows, onboarding and checkout across web and mobile. As a Test Engineer here, you won't hand down verdicts after the fact; you'll build the capability that lets verification happen without you in the room. The engineering discipline bar is the same as any software role: version control, review in both directions, CI, design before implementation, and root-cause debugging by the owner. The Test Engineer will be integral part of the team and takes pride in advocating for the quality of the Zettle mobile app on Android and iOS, along with the backend and web services behind it. Meet our team: Zettle is PayPal's point-of-sale and payments product for small businesses. Zettle India is part of the Payment Services and Crypto organization, and our test engineering team supports the Zettle mobile app on Android and iOS and the services behind it. We are a centralized Test and Quality Engineering function actively moving to an automation-first, shift-left culture. You will be joining a growing team and help shape its test strategy, automation framework, and quality standards. You will partner closely with developers and product managers, and mentor engineers in the team. This is a hybrid role based in Bangalore, with three days a week onsite. Your way to impact: As a Test Engineer, you will help make sure that merchants can take payments without problems on any device. You will own testing for the features you work on, from test planning to release, and you will help move our testing from manual to automated over time. Your work will reduce production defects, speed up releases, and improve the experience of small businesses that use Zettle every day. You will grow toward a Senior Test Engineer role as you build your technical depth and ownership. Test APIs and backend services using Postman or RestAssured and validate data using SQL queries. Familiarity with Jenkins, BrowserStack, and debugging tools such as Logcat and the Xcode console. Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to work with developers and product managers. Ownership, curiosity, and a willingness to learn. Nice to have: Appium, Kotlin or Swift reading ability, mobile performance testing (Android Profiler, Xcode Instruments), JMeter, AWS, and experience in payments or FinTech. description: Itron is innovating new ways for utilities and cities to manage energy and water. We create a more resourceful world to protect essential resources for today and tomorrow. Join us. Your tickets, customer updates and escalations are short, precise and easy to act on, for both customers and engineers. You stay calm under pressure. You've handled urgent, high-visibility issues and kept customers informed while you worked them. You work with minimal handholding. You take an issue, work it to the end, and know when and how to escalate. Availability: comfortable working hours that overlap with US customers. Sense of Urgency : Knows the importance of resolving customer issue asap or knowns when to escalate and when to protect engineering Team Bandwidth. We care how you solve problems more than which ticketing tool you used. Technical background You've supported web-based software running in the cloud, with hands-on skills such as: SQL: you write queries confidently to investigate data issues and verify fixes. APIs: you can call and debug REST APIs with tools such as Postman or curl, and read request and response payloads. Logs and monitoring: you've searched logs and dashboards in tools such as CloudWatch, Datadog, Splunk or Kibana to trace an issue. Cloud: working knowledge of AWS or another cloud — enough to understand where a service runs and what can fail. Scripting: basic Python, Bash or similar to automate checks and repetitive fixes. Support tooling: ticketing and incident tools such as Jira, Zendesk, Freshdesk or PagerDuty, and the discipline of SLAs and priorities. Exact tools matter less than depth. Strong experience on an equivalent stack is welcome. What sets great candidates apart Impact you can explain. Resolution time went down, escalations to engineering dropped, or a recurring issue disappeared — and you can say what you did. A hard case, told in detail. An issue others gave up on that you traced to its root cause across logs, data and code. Ticket killers. You've turned repeat issues into a runbook, a script, a KB article or a product fix, so they stopped coming in. Incident experience. You've been part of a major outage or peak event and helped keep customers informed while it was fixed. Trusted by engineers. Developers took your escalations seriously because your diagnosis was usually right. What we look for in everyone we hire Whatever the role, we hire for six things. Customer obsession. You treat every ticket as a customer who can't do their job, and you follow up until it's actually solved. Impact over activity. You measure success by problems solved and tickets prevented, not tickets touched. Honesty. You tell customers what you know and what you don't, never promise what engineering hasn't committed, and own your mistakes. Independence. You don't wait to be told what to do next. You work an issue to the end with little hand-holding. You will work with leaders who will partner with you in the journey. Passion. Not the word on a resume — the evidence: a tool you built to make support faster, a product you learned inside out, things you taught others. Depth. At least one product you've supported well enough to explain how it works under the hood and where it usually breaks. Itron is committed to building an inclusive and diverse workforce and providing an authentic workplace experience for all employees.
